note: Five additional CRE Set 3 items. Not copied from Set 2. Each display equation is on its own line.

questions.stem:
Life follows a Weibull distribution with shape \(\beta\) and characteristic life \(\eta\). Use \(e^{-0.125}=0.8825\).
\[
R(t)=\exp\left[-(t/\eta)^{\beta}\right]
\]
What is the reliability at 150 hours?
questions.why: Cube the time ratio, then use the given exponential. Do not stop at the ratio. \[ (150/300)^{3}=0.125 \] \[ R(150)=\exp(-0.125)=0.8825 \] 0.125 is the Weibull exponent. 0.500 is the time ratio. 0.1175 is the unreliability. C. 0.8825

chart.title: Weibull life
chart.altText: The shape is 3 and the characteristic life is 300 hours. Reliability is asked at 150 hours.

questions.stem:
Two different units are in active parallel. Either unit can carry the function, and the units fail independently.
\[
R_s=1-(1-R_1)(1-R_2)
\]
What is the mission reliability of the pair?
questions.why: The pair fails only when both units fail. \[ (1-0.75)(1-0.60)=0.100 \] \[ R_s=1-0.100=0.900 \] 0.450 is the product of the two reliabilities. 0.675 is their average. 0.750 is the stronger unit alone. D. 0.900

chart.title: Two-unit active parallel
chart.altText: Unit 1 has mission reliability 0.75. Unit 2 has mission reliability 0.60. Either unit can carry the function.

questions.stem:
Five independent trials each have failure probability \(p\). The count of failures is binomial.
\[
P(X=2)=\binom{5}{2}p^{2}(1-p)^{3}
\]
What is the probability of exactly two failures?
questions.why: Include the number of ways to place the two failures. \[ \binom{5}{2}=10 \] \[ P(X=2)=10(0.20)^{2}(0.80)^{3}=0.2048 \] 0.0205 is one specific sequence. 0.3277 is the probability of zero failures. 0.8000 is the probability that one trial succeeds. B. 0.2048

traps.C: Computes the probability of no failures.

chart.title: Five independent trials
chart.altText: Each trial has failure probability 0.20. The trials are independent.

questions.stem:
Users split between two operating modes. The failure intensity of the product is the weighted average of the mode intensities.
\[
\lambda=0.70\lambda_A+0.30\lambda_B
\]
What is the failure intensity?
questions.why: Weight each mode by its share of use. \[ 0.70(0.010)=0.007 \] \[ 0.30(0.040)=0.012 \] \[ \lambda=0.007+0.012=0.019 \] 0.010 is mode A alone. 0.025 is the unweighted average. 0.040 is mode B alone. A. 0.019 per hour

traps.B: Uses only the larger user group.
traps.C: Averages the two intensities with equal weights.

chart.title: Operational profile
chart.altText: Seventy percent of use is in mode A, where the failure intensity is 0.010 per hour. Thirty percent is in mode B, where it is 0.040 per hour.

questions.stem:
A series system has a failure-rate goal \(\lambda_s\). The goal is split equally across \(m\) elements.
\[
\lambda_i=\frac{\lambda_s}{m}
\]
What failure rate is allocated to each element?
questions.why: Divide the system goal by the number of elements. Do not multiply. \[ \lambda_i=0.0012/4=0.0003 \] 0.0012 is the system goal. 0.0048 multiplies the goal by 4. 4 is the element count. A. 0.0003 per hour

traps.C: Multiplies the goal by the element count.

chart.title: Equal failure-rate allocation
chart.altText: The series system failure-rate goal is 0.0012 per hour. It is split equally across 4 elements.
